title: DPT-DDPM: A Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Tabular Data
summary: Applies denoising diffusion to tabular generation and compares the result against the GAN generation that preceded it. CTGAN is one of the baselines run, with its output distributions plotted against the real wilt dataset.
evidence: CTGAN listed as a conditional GAN-based baseline; figure 2 shows the feature distributions of the wilt dataset for the real data and the data generated by CTGAN

title: Validity of Synthetic Tabular Data Using Rules
summary: Asks whether generated tables obey the rules the real data obeys, which distributional scores do not capture, and tests the popular generators against explicit constraints. TVAE and CTGAN are the deep-learning generators chosen for the comparison.
evidence: for the deep learning group, we have chosen TVAE and CTGAN; the popular tabular synthetic data generators have been the focus of this work

title: Interpretable Data-Driven Approach Based on Feature Selection Methods and GAN-Based Models for Cardiovascular Risk Prediction in Diabetic Patients
summary: Predicts cardiovascular risk in diabetic patients by pairing feature selection with generated data, keeping the model interpretable enough to inspect. The published code is released as cvd-risk-fs-ctgan, naming CTGAN as the generator behind the oversampling the paper describes.
evidence: the paper's released code is github.com/ai4healthurjc/cvd-risk-fs-ctgan; section 'C. Oversampling Methods' describes GAN-based synthetic sample generation
needs: the body describes the oversampling as GAN-based without naming CTGAN in prose; the attribution rests on the repository name and the reference list

title: Moving Conditional GAN Close to Data: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation and Its Experimental Evaluation
summary: Proposes a conditional GAN variant for tabular synthesis and evaluates it against both augmentation algorithms and other generative models across ten runs. CTGAN sits among the state-of-the-art generative models the accuracy comparison is drawn against.
evidence: Table V: accuracy comparison of the proposed method versus existing SOTA generative models, averaged over ten tests

title: SiloFuse: Cross-silo Synthetic Data Generation with Latent Tabular Diffusion Models
summary: Generates tabular data across silos that cannot pool their records, using latent diffusion rather than a GAN so no raw features cross a boundary. CTGAN and TVAE are among the generators the quantitative analysis measures against.
evidence: section 'C. Quantitative Analysis' compares against the baseline generators, CTGAN and TVAE among them
